title: Preservation for a general separated finite-type morphism
statement:
Fix the purity coefficient conventions [def-pur-conventions]:
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$,
a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $n\geq1$, with
$A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type
$k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism
[def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the
constructible exceptional inverse image $Rf^!$ of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], whose adjunction relative to the
bounded constructible coefficient class is supplied by
[cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]; no unrestricted ambient exceptional
right adjoint datum is assumed. Then the analogues of the two preservation
clauses (2) and (3) of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] hold
for this functor, with the following bounds.

If $X$ is nonempty, choose the finite affine charts
$U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and closed presentations
$U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility], with affine space understood as in
[def-sbc-affine-space], omitting empty charts. Put
$$
D=\max_U d_U,\qquad c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y),\qquad
c=\max_U\bigl(c_U+1+2(D-d_U)\bigr).
$$
Here dimension is Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension].
If $X$ is empty, put $D=c=0$ instead; there are no chart constants
$c_U$ to form (in particular no dimension of an empty $Y$ is needed).
For every pair of integers $a\leq b$:

1. $Rf^!$ carries $D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ into
$D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A)$, with constructible intervals as in
[def-weil-constructible-intervals].
2. If $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, then
$Rf^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,A)$ has Tor amplitude in
$[a-2D,b-2D+c]$, in the sense of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: At the actual quotient A=O_E/(varpi^n), ell belongs to the maximal ideal because its extended ell-adic norm is less than one. The maximal ideal is generated by varpi, so ell^n is zero in A. Since ell differs from the characteristic of the finite-field datum, ell^n is a unit on Y. Install HasInvertibleExponent for the standard ULift of A. Finite-type Y has finite Krull dimension, giving the bound sfDimension Y.

proof.text: For a closed immersion i:Z -> T over a field, use the supported localization triangle. The complement has dimension at most d, and this bound persists under field extension by topologicalKrullDim_pullback_le. The published torsion direct-image vanishing theorem bounds Rj_* on sheaves by 2d. Finite truncation devissage bounds Rj_*j^* on [a,b] by [a,b+2d]. The triangle and exact closed pullback give Ri^! the interval [a,b+2d+1]. This is closed_homology, written from the published supportedLocalizationTriangle and amplitude API.

proof.text: For a smooth projection of relative dimension n, smooth tensor duality identifies its exceptional inverse image with exact pullback tensored with a flat rank-one sheaf shifted by 2n. Thus smooth_homology shifts both endpoints by -2n. On an affine chart U -> A^n_V -> V -> Y, the ambient dimension is at most dim Y+n. Compose the ordinary etale exceptional functors and apply the closed bound: the chart interval is [a-2n,b+2 dim Y+1]. Bounded constructibility is supplied by the published boundedConstructible_rightDerivedUpperShriek. For Tor amplitude use the existing source-library theorem constructibleTorAmplitudeIn_rightDerivedUpperShriek_chart, which proves exactly the smooth/closed chart assertion with the same endpoints.

proof.text: Flatten the finite source charts using the finite sigma type and equivFin. Each point is covered by target_cover and source_cover. Composition and the equality presentation_over identify the restricted exceptional image with its closed/smooth chart factorization. Each chart dimension is at most maxDimension by Finset.le_sup, so widen lower endpoints to a-2 maxDimension. Apply the published homologyConcentratedIn_of_openCover and constructibleTorAmplitudeIn_of_openCover. Apply this to nonemptyCharts, and rewrite the upper endpoint using b-2D+(2D+2 dim Y+1)=b+2 dim Y+1. For empty X use the empty finite cover; all local obligations are eliminated by Fin.elim0, including constructibility and Tor amplitude.

proof.text: A bounded constructible pro-etale input is isomorphic to the exact comparison pullback of an etale bounded constructible G. Exact comparison preserves and reflects its cohomological interval, and the comparison Tor theorem preserves and reflects the same Tor interval. The derived comparison unit on G is an isomorphism. By the defining formula nu_X^* f^! Rnu_Y,* of the exceptional functor, map that unit through the etale exceptional functor and then nu_X^*. Transport the etale output bounds and constructibility across this isomorphism. Package bounded constructibility and the displayed Tor interval as constructibleFiniteTor. Specialize to the actual quotient and the supplied compactification; no ambient pro-etale adjunction is assumed.

blueprint_update.statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter
([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $f:X\to Y$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism. The ambient exceptional right adjoint datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is not assumed: on the bounded
constructible and finite-Tor coefficients of the two clauses below it is the
theorem [cor-sf-ambient-adjoint-discharge]. Then $f$
satisfies the two preservation clauses of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility]: with the affine charts
$U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and the integers $d_U$ of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility], put
$D=\max_Ud_U$ and $c_U=2\,(d_U+\dim Y)$. Then $Rf^!$ carries
$D_c^{[a,b]}(Y,A)$ into $D_c^{[a-2D,b-2D+c]}(X,A)$ for
$c=\max_U\bigl(c_U+1+2(D-d_U)\bigr)$, and it carries finite Tor
amplitude in $[a,b]$ to finite Tor amplitude in $[a-2D,b-2D+c]$.

proof.text:
For each chart the target $\mathbf A^{d_U}_V$ of the chartwise
presentation is of finite type over $k$ of dimension
$d_U+\dim V\leq d_U+\dim Y$. The open complement $W_U$ of $U$ in it
therefore satisfies the open-complement condition with constant
$2(d_U+\dim V)$ by [lem-exc-open-complement-known], hence also with
the larger constant $c_U=2(d_U+\dim Y)$, the condition being monotone
in its constant. The hypothesis of
[thm-pur-general-admissibility] is thus satisfied with these
constants, and its conclusion is the assertion.
